Model-averaged posterior draws and predictions across mvgam fits

Source: R/pp_average.mvgam.R
posterior_average.mvgam.Rd

Bayesian model averaging of two or more mvgam fits, as in brms::posterior_average.brmsfit() and brms::pp_average.brmsfit(). Each fit contributes draws in proportion to its model weight. posterior_average() averages parameter draws. pp_average() averages predictions.

Usage

# S3 method for mvgam
posterior_average(
  x,
  ...,
  variable = NULL,
  pars = NULL,
  weights = "stacking",
  ndraws = NULL,
  nsamples = NULL,
  missing = NULL,
  model_names = NULL,
  control = list(),
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for mvgam
pp_average(
  x,
  ...,
  weights = "stacking",
  method = "posterior_predict",
  ndraws = NULL,
  nsamples = NULL,
  summary = TRUE,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
  robust = FALSE,
  model_names = NULL,
  control = list(),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A fitted mvgam object. Further fits are passed via ....

...

Further fitted mvgam objects to average over. For pp_average(), named arguments are passed to the prediction function method names.

variable

Optional character vector of parameter names to extract, as variables.mvgam() lists them. A bare vector name selects every element. NULL (the default) selects all parameters shared across fits (or all parameters across the union when missing is supplied), excluding "lp__".

pars

Deprecated brms alias for variable.

weights

A numeric vector with one weight per fit, scaled to sum to one, or one of "stacking", "pseudobma", "pseudobma+", "loo" and "waic". mvgam_loo_extras describes each.

ndraws

Total number of model-averaged draws to return. Defaults to the number of draws in the first fit.

nsamples

Deprecated brms alias for ndraws.

missing

Values for parameters some fits lack. NULL (the default) restricts variable to the parameters every fit has and refuses a name outside them. A list keyed by parameter name gives each parameter its own value. A single number fills every parameter a fit lacks.

model_names

Optional character vector of model labels; overrides the names inferred from the call.

control

A list of extra arguments passed to loo::loo_model_weights() when computing stacking / pseudo-BMA weights.

seed

Optional integer seed. The session's random state is restored when the call returns.

method

Which prediction function pp_average() calls on each fit before averaging: "posterior_predict" (the default), "posterior_epred" or "posterior_linpred".

summary

Logical. If TRUE (the default), pp_average() summarises the averaged predictions with posterior_summary.mvgam() as a mean, an error and two quantiles. FALSE returns the averaged draws.

probs

Numeric vector of probabilities for quantile computation. Default is c(0.025, 0.975) for 95% credible intervals. Can be a single value or multiple values.

robust

Logical. If FALSE (the default), uses mean and standard deviation for summaries. If TRUE, uses median and median absolute deviation (MAD).

Value

posterior_average() returns a data.frame of model-averaged posterior draws. pp_average() returns a numeric matrix of averaged predictions. With summary = TRUE its rows are observations and its columns summary statistics. Otherwise its rows are draws and its columns observations. Attribute weights

holds the weight of each fit. Attribute ndraws holds the number of draws taken from each fit.

See also

loo_model_weights.mvgam() computes the weights. ensemble() averages forecasts. The forecast evaluation article weights and combines competing models.

Other model comparison: bridge_sampler.mvgam(), compare_elpds(), kfold.mvgam(), lfo_cv.mvgam(), log_lik.mvgam(), loo.mvgam(), loo_compare.mvgam_lfo(), mvgam_loo_extras, waic.mvgam()

Nicholas J Clark

Examples

# \dontrun{
# Two models of one count series: with and without a smooth of x
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                    n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
mod1 <- mvgam(y ~ s(x), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
              data   = simdat$data_train, family = poisson(),
              chains = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 9 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
mod2 <- update(mod1, formula = y ~ 1)

# Stacking weights from approximate leave-one-out cross-validation
loo_model_weights(mod1, mod2)
#> Warning: Some Pareto k diagnostic values are too high. See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.
#> Warning: Some Pareto k diagnostic values are too high. See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.
#> Method: stacking
#> ------
#>      weight
#> mod1 0.926 
#> mod2 0.074 

# The trend coefficient, averaged over both fits under those weights
pa <- posterior_average(mod1, mod2, variable = "ar1_trend")
#> Warning: Some Pareto k diagnostic values are too high. See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.
#> Warning: Some Pareto k diagnostic values are too high. See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.
attr(pa, "weights")
#>       mod1       mod2 
#> 0.92564222 0.07435778 
summary(pa)
#>  ar1_trend[series_1]
#>  Min.   :-0.1822    
#>  1st Qu.: 0.4631    
#>  Median : 0.5853    
#>  Mean   : 0.5647    
#>  3rd Qu.: 0.6855    
#>  Max.   : 0.9679    

# Averaged expected counts, one row per observation
head(pp_average(mod1, mod2, method = "posterior_epred"))
#> Warning: Some Pareto k diagnostic values are too high. See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.
#> Warning: Some Pareto k diagnostic values are too high. See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.
#>       Estimate Est.Error     Q2.5     Q97.5
#> [1,]  2.220143 0.9566231 1.180168  5.300869
#> [2,] 13.724705 4.0070239 4.820149 21.422211
#> [3,]  7.630045 1.6181153 4.793008 10.849862
#> [4,]  8.091060 1.9292548 4.790454 12.014596
#> [5,]  4.875531 1.1104207 3.014174  7.344376
#> [6,]  7.089481 2.4584061 3.878689 12.517647
# }
